questions.q: What is the difference between a SQL Server "version" and an "edition"?
options: Version refers to the OS; edition refers to SQL Server
Edition determines the release year; version determines the feature tier
Version is when it was released (2019, 2022); edition is the licensed feature tier (Enterprise, Standard, etc.)
They are two names for the exact same thing
questions.explain: Version determines the feature baseline for a release; edition determines feature caps within that version through licensing.

questions.q: Which edition is functionally identical to Enterprise but licensed only for development and testing, never production?
questions.explain: Developer edition has the full Enterprise feature set for free, but its license prohibits production use.

questions.q: Which Enterprise-only feature lets a large index be rebuilt without blocking concurrent access to the table?
questions.explain: On Standard, an index rebuild takes an exclusive lock for its duration; Enterprise's Online Index Rebuild keeps the table available throughout.

questions.q: What T-SQL would you run to check the edition of a running instance?
questions.explain: SERVERPROPERTY('Edition') returns the running instance's edition; @@VERSION covers the version and build details.

questions.q: Why does Standard edition's memory cap matter in practice?
options: A Standard-edition server with a large amount of RAM installed may only be able to use a fraction of it for the Database Engine
Standard edition has no memory cap, unlike Enterprise
Standard edition cannot use any RAM at all
The memory cap only affects SQL Server Agent, not the Database Engine
questions.explain: Standard caps how much memory the Database Engine can use, well below Enterprise's effectively unlimited ceiling, regardless of how much physical RAM is installed.
